c.tagline: Germany's car capital, cradled by vineyards and wooded hills.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; Free Now and Uber dispatch the same licensed taxis, so prices are broadly similar and there is little street-hailing outside ranks and stations.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Klett-Passage underpass at the main station attracts drinkers late at night, and pickpockets work the Volksfest and Christmas market crowds.

hood_desc: The walkable core around Schlossplatz, the Konigstrasse shopping boulevard, the palaces and the main museums; where first-timers stay to have everything on foot and the Hauptbahnhof on the doorstep.
A leafy, elegant residential quarter of Gruenderzeit apartment blocks, neighborhood cafes and the pretty Feuersee church, a short walk or Stadtbahn hop from the center; calm but well-connected.
A younger, trendier district around Marienplatz and the Heusteigviertel, packed with bars, indie cafes, the Zacke rack railway and a lively going-out scene.
Stuttgart's oldest surviving quarter, a cluster of narrow lanes once home to tanners and winegrowers, now full of galleries, boutiques, workshops and traditional wine taverns (Besenwirtschaften).

A spa and heritage district across the Neckar with Europe's second-richest mineral springs, the Wilhelma zoo and botanical garden, the Mercedes-Benz Museum and the giant Cannstatter Wasen festival grounds.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Stadtbahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4:30am-1am; night buses and weekend night trains cover the small hours on Friday and Saturday.
transit.pay: No transit card needed: buy tickets in the VVS mobile app or from station machines (bank cards accepted) and keep them for inspection. A single ride is about 3 EUR (~US$3.30) and a day ticket around 6 EUR; one ticket covers the Stadtbahn, S-Bahn and buses across the zones you buy. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (58 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

transit.m: S-Bahn S2 or S3 to Hauptbahnhof (~27 min)

tip.r: 5-10% / round up the bill for good service

landmarks: Fernsehturm Stuttgart
The world's first concrete-shaft television tower offers a dramatic silhouette and panoramic views over Stuttgart's hills and vineyards.
Schlossplatz
Stuttgart's grand central square, framed by the Neues Schloss and Jubiläumssäule column, is the beating heart of the city's public life.
Neues Schloss (New Palace)
This opulent 18th-century Baroque palace anchors Schlossplatz and is one of the most photographed facades in the city.
Altes Schloss (Old Castle)
A moated Renaissance castle dating to the 10th century, home to the Württemberg State Museum and a picturesque inner courtyard.
Stiftskirche (Stuttgart Collegiate Church)
The city's historic mother church, with its two asymmetrical towers, is a striking Gothic landmark in the old town.
Mercedes-Benz Museum
A spiraling, futuristic architectural icon housing the story of the automobile, instantly recognizable on Stuttgart's skyline.
Porsche Museum
A sleek, angular building showcasing decades of Porsche sports cars, a must for architecture and auto enthusiasts alike.
Wilhelma Zoological and Botanical Garden
A unique blend of Moorish-style pavilions, gardens, and one of Europe's most diverse zoos in a single striking setting.
Schloss Solitude
A hilltop Rococo palace with sweeping views over the Stuttgart region, epitomizing 18th-century elegance.
Stuttgart City Library (Stadtbibliothek)
A minimalist cube-shaped building with a glowing blue-white interior atrium that has become a favorite subject for photographers.

train.note: Stuttgart Hbf is in the middle of a decade-long rebuild into an underground through-station (Stuttgart 21), so expect diversions and changed platforms - check departures on the day. The Paris TGV takes about 3h10 and Zurich around 3 hours. Nightjet sleepers run toward Austria and Italy. DB's Sparpreis fares open six months ahead and are far cheaper than walk-up.

intl.to: Paris, Prague, Vienna, Zurich & across Europe

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the SAB terminal at Stuttgart Airport rather than the main station - allow 30 minutes on the S-Bahn to get there. FlixBus dominates, with Munich about 3 hours away and Paris around 8. Carry your passport or EU ID card for cross-border services.

ferry.note: Stuttgart is inland on the Neckar, which carries freight barges but no scheduled passenger service, so there are no ferries. Excursion boats run short trips from Bad Cannstatt in summer.
